name.text: Shared: Interpret the intersection of two service plans

questiontext.text:
Two service providers offer different payment plans.

Plan A has a lower starting fee but charges more for each service unit.

Plan B has a higher starting fee but charges less for each service unit.

Their total costs are shown on the graph below.

[[jsxgraph]] JXG.Options.text.useMathJax = true; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard( divid, { axis: true, showCopyright: false, boundingbox: [-1,45,8,-5], keepaspectratio: false, grid: true } ); var planA = board.create( 'functiongraph', [ function(x) { return {#mA#}*x + {#bA#}; } ], { fixed: true, strokeWidth: 3 } ); var planB = board.create( 'functiongraph', [ function(x) { return {#mB#}*x + {#bB#}; } ], { fixed: true, strokeWidth: 3, dash: 2 } ); board.create( 'text', [ 5.4, 39, 'Plan A' ], { fixed: true } ); board.create( 'text', [ 5.4, 35, 'Plan B' ], { fixed: true } ); board.unsuspendUpdate(); [[/jsxgraph]]

The two graphs intersect at one point.

Interpret that intersection in the context of the service plans.

At [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] service units, both plans have a total cost of [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] credits. [[feedback:prt1]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

The graphs intersect at \[ ({@xI@},{@yI@}). \]

The horizontal coordinate tells us the number of service units. Therefore, \[ x={@xI@}. \]

The vertical coordinate tells us the total cost. Therefore, \[ y={@yI@}. \]

So the intersection means:

At {@xI@} service units, both plans cost {@yI@} credits.

intersection-interpretation

Learners inspect two linear cost relationships and interpret both coordinates of their intersection in the real-world context.

Unlike QLIN-08, the learner is not asked to report the intersection as an ordered pair. The learner must explain what the horizontal and vertical coordinates mean in the situation.

Adapted from the straight-line graph question family represented by Numbas question NUMBAS-17290, "Graphs I: Linear - Line equation", licensed CC BY 4.0. The service-plan context, generated relationships, contextual prompts and diagnostic grading are independently written for QLIN-09.

node.description: Checks interpretation of the horizontal coordinate.

truefeedback.text: Correct. The horizontal coordinate represents the number of service units.

node.description: Detects use of the cost coordinate as the number of service units.

truefeedback.text: You appear to have used the total cost as the number of service units. The horizontal coordinate tells us how many service units are used.

falsefeedback.text: Read the horizontal coordinate of the point where the two cost graphs meet. That coordinate represents the number of service units.

node.description: Checks interpretation of the vertical coordinate.

truefeedback.text: Correct. The vertical coordinate represents the common total cost.

node.description: Detects use of the service-unit coordinate as the total cost.

truefeedback.text: You appear to have used the number of service units as the total cost. The vertical coordinate tells us the cost shared by both plans at the intersection.

falsefeedback.text: Read the vertical coordinate of the point where the two graphs meet. That coordinate represents the common total cost.

qtest.description: The generated contextual interpretation should receive full credit.
